SMTO-EXE-0111 — SMTO can't find that browser tab

GUID: 78031f62-7d39-5b6b-a9ff-74f9886101cc
Slug: browser-tab-not-found
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • SMTO tried to work in a browser tab it no longer recognizes, for example one that was closed or belongs to another browser window. Nothing was done in the page by this step.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In this conversation, ask SMTO: "List the open tabs in your browser and continue in the right one." The list contains only tabs that exist right now, so SMTO can pick a real one.
  2. If the page you need is not in the list, ask SMTO to open a new tab and go to that page's web address. The tab SMTO remembered may have been closed, so opening the page again gives it a fresh tab.
  3. If a browser window SMTO opened is visible on the Gateway computer, leave its tabs open until SMTO is finished. Closing a tab by hand removes it from SMTO's list of tabs it can use.

What success looks like

  • SMTO names the tab it is using, and the expected page is shown in it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to repeat form actions until you've checked the page in the correct tab.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The browser operation's tab_id does not match any tab tracked for the current browser session on the Gateway.

What this means

  • The supplied tab ID did not match a tab in the synchronized current session. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • The supplied tab ID did not match a tab in the synchronized current session.

How to diagnose it

  • List tabs in that exact session and compare the requested ID rather than guessing from a URL or title.

How to fix it

  • PlaywrightBackend.execute looked up args['tab_id'] in session.tabs after _sync_tabs and found no match. Call browser.tabs for the same browser_session_id and use an exact returned tab_id, or browser.open_tab to create one; tab IDs are not shared between sessions.
  • Use browser.tabs and select an exact tab ID in the same session.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use browser.tabs and select an exact tab ID in the same session.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended tab resolves under the same owned session.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
